strategies.overview: Tornadus's high-Base Power STAB and coverage moves, which are both further bolstered by its gargantuan offenses, and access to amazing utility options like Knock Off and Taunt make it a versatile threat in NU. Its Speed is also enormous, letting it blow past common fast Pokemon like Alolan Ninetales, Munkidori, and Paldean Tauros-W. On top of that, it has access to two amazing abilities that allow it to either be more supportive by getting off a fast Taunt and setting up Rain Dance freely with Prankster or offensive by letting it take advantage of common stat-dropping moves and abilities like Altaria's Defog, Brambleghast's Strength Sap, and both Paldean Tauros-W's and Incineroar's Intimidate. While some Tornadus sets run Heavy-Duty Boots, a fair amount don't, since other items can provide more support at times. Tornadus's weakness to Stealth Rock is further exacerbated on non-Heavy-Duty Boots sets by how much it loves to repeatedly come in, though. As a trade-off for its great offensive prowess, Tornadus has low bulk, which really starts to show when combined with its Stealth Rock weakness, and because of it, Tornadus's useful resistances and immunities are rendered moot, meaning it can be overpowered by Flamigo's Close Combat or KOed by a secondary STAB move like Flygon's Outrage. Tornadus also has to deal with either using unreliable moves like Hurricane and Bleakwind Storm or dealing with adverse contact effects such as paralysis from Bellibolt's Static. Not only that, but Amoonguss, Galarian Slowbro, and Bellibolt often carry Rocky Helmet, worsening Tornadus's situation.
strategies.comments:
Other Options

Sludge Bomb allows Tornadus to threaten Fairy-types like Sylveon, Florges, and Tera Fairy Galarian Slowbro, and it can usefully spread poison; however, Tornadus's other moves tend to provide more utility overall. Bulk Up sets can opt for Rest + Chesto Berry alongside Prankster so that they can set up many more times, but losing out on Defiant is quite detrimental with how common Intimidate is. A Choice Specs set with Hurricane / Focus Blast / Dark Pulse / U-turn can be run with Tornadus's enormous Special Attack and Speed as well as its access to pivoting, but its reliance on inaccurate moves can make it inconsistent at times. Tornadus can trade out Rain Dance and Damp Rock for Snowscape, Sunny Day, or Sandstorm and its respective weather-elongating item depending on what weather team it's being run on, but non-rain weather teams aren't as consistent overall.

Checks and Counters

Electric-types: Bellibolt, Rotom-H, Raikou, and Kilowattrel all can take on Tornadus's Hurricane and Acrobatics and retaliate with super effective STAB attacks. On top of that, they can all use Tornadus for momentum, Bellibolt can spread status with Toxic, Rotom-H and Raikou can set up, and Raikou and Kilowattrel outspeed it naturally. However, they can be easily caught off-guard by Tera Ground, and Bellibolt and Raikou must be wary of Tera Blast Ground.

Steel-types: Copperajah, Registeel, and Bronzong can take multiple hits from Tornadus, and they can capitalize on this by setting up entry hazards or boosting their stats. However, the former two need to watch out for common super effective coverage moves, the latter needs to be cautious of Knock Off, and they all have to watch out for Heat Wave.

Rock-types: Minior, Drednaw, and Diancie can use Tornadus as setup fodder or an opportunity to set up their hazards. However, the latter two need to watch out for super effective coverage moves.

Ice-types: While Alolan Ninetales isn't insanely bulky, it can almost always take one attack from Tornadus, especially from physically oriented sets, and retaliate with a powerful Blizzard. Alolan Ninetales also sets snow, forcing Tornadus to set up rain again. Similarly, physical Tornadus sets struggle to get past Avalugg. However, special attacking Tornadus sets with moves like Hurricane, Bleakwind Storm, and Heat Wave can get past Avalugg without too much of an issue.

Stealth Rock: Tornadus tends to prefer items other than Heavy-Duty Boots, as they can provide more utility. However, this causes Stealth Rock to be an enormous issue, and with how often certain Tornadus sets love to switch in and out, the damage can rack up quickly.

movesets.name: Offensive Pivot
movesets.description:
Set Details

Bleakwind Storm is preferred due to its higher accuracy; however, Hurricane is a stronger STAB move to fire off. Knock Off cripples common switch-ins like Bronzong, Brambleghast, and Diancie. Heat Wave lets Tornadus nail Steel-types like Copperajah, Bronzong, and Registeel, while Grass Knot allows Tornadus to hit Ground- and Water-types like Gastrodon and Milotic. On the other hand, Taunt lets Tornadus stop walls like Bronzong, Gligar, and Gastrodon from setting up, getting their entry hazards up, or healing. An alternative EV spread of 116 HP / 140 SpA / 252 Spe can be used to survive common Choice Scarf users' attacks like Chandelure's Overheat and Hisuian Typhlosion's Eruption. Tera Steel allows Tornadus to tank a variety of hits like Cinccino's Tail Slap, Munkidori's Sludge Wave, and Sylveon's Hyper Voice. Alternatively, Tera Ground lets Tornadus take an Electric- or Rock-type attack from Kilowattrel and Diancie.

Tornadus excels at firing off Knock Off and pivoting out, so entry hazard setters like Gastrodon, Bronzong, Orthworm, and Diancie can help capitalize on this trait. Tornadus can take one or two Fighting-type attacks, but it can't switch in consistently. Because of this, Fighting-resistant partners like Galarian Slowbro, Scream Tail, and Sylveon pair well with it. Pivots like Inteleon, Milotic, and Flygon enjoy Tornadus's presence, as it can easily dismantle common Grass-type switch-ins like Decidueye, Amoonguss, and Breloom. Ground- and Steel-types such as Gligar, Gastrodon, Bronzong, and Orthworm can help take on Electric- and Rock-types like Kilowattrel and Diancie that threaten Tornadus. As Tornadus typically lures in Rock-, Electric-, and Steel-types like Diancie, Bellibolt, and Registeel, wallbreakers like Basculegion-M, Choice Band Flygon, Guts Heracross, and Swords Dance Incineroar that capitalize on these Pokemon as entry points synergize extremely well; on top of that, they can also get rid of any neutral special walls trying to check Tornadus like Alolan Muk, Milotic, and Assault Vest Galarian Slowbro.

movesets.name: Rain Setter
movesets.description:
Set Details

U-turn allows Tornadus to bring in a rain sweeper, and it can help create mind games with opposing leads like Galvantula and Cinccino; however, Taunt stops setup sweepers and entry hazard setters from taking advantage of Tornadus. Under rain, Weather Ball is a powerful move that hits Flying-resistant Pokemon like Diancie super effectively while providing strong neutral coverage for others like Copperajah, but Knock Off allows Tornadus to provide more utility, removing important items like Leftovers and Heavy-Duty Boots while hitting Bronzong and Wind Rider Brambleghast super effectively. Tera Steel provides a strong defensive typing that can let Tornadus have an easier time both setting up rain and pivoting. On the other hand, Tera Ground can turn the tables against Electric- and Rock-types like Kilowattrel and Diancie, which would threaten Tornadus otherwise.

Basculegion-M is a no-brainer when it comes to partners, as it can take advantage of Tornadus's rain-setting capabilities with its Swift Swim and rain-boosted Water-type STAB attacks. Other Swift Swim users like Kingdra, Overqwil, and Ludicolo also pair well while offering unique qualities: Kingdra excels at weakening Water-resistant and -immune Pokemon; Overqwil offers rain teams an easy way to handle Grass-types; and Ludicolo takes advantage of Water-types that rain teams can struggle with like Vaporeon, Gastrodon, and Milotic while acting as a secondary rain setter. As Tornadus is quite offensive, it tends to not have great longevity, so a more defensive rain setter like Klefki is greatly appreciated. On top of being more reliable, Klefki can support its team with both entry hazards and Thunder Wave. Tornadus can't handle Water-types too well, and neither can most Swift Swim users; thus, partners like Toxicroak, Kilowattrel, and Brambleghast are greatly appreciated.

movesets.name: Bulk Up
movesets.description:
Set Details

Hammer Arm is the preferred option to take out Steel-types like Copperajah, Registeel, and Tera Steel Sylveon due to its high Base Power, but because of how it drops Tornadus's Speed, Brick Break can be used for a less punishing but weaker alternative. Notably, at +1, Tornadus's Hammer Arm OHKOes Copperajah after one layer of Spikes and 2HKOes both Registeel and Orthworm. Tera Blast Ground gives Tornadus a more reliable way to take out the aforementioned Steel-types, barring Orthworm, along with Rock-types like Diancie. Tera Ground also allows Tornadus to surprise and take hits from Kilowattrel and Diancie. Alternatively, Knock Off can be used so that Tornadus neither has to Terastallize nor drop its Speed if it wishes to hit or take out Steel-types on low health, and it gives Tornadus a way to easily deal with Bronzong. Sitrus Berry provides some recovery to Tornadus and, when consumed, allows Acrobatics to be at full power. However, no item can be run to automatically have Tornadus at its fullest potential. Defiant lets Tornadus take advantage of common stat-dropping abilities and moves like Overqwil's and Incineroar's Intimidate as well as Vileplume's Strength Sap. Tera Steel can be run to gift Tornadus with a typing that better handles common special attackers like Munkidori, Dragalge, and Sylveon that could easily break through it.

Since Defiant is Bulk Up Tornadus's biggest draw, leads like Galvantula, Brambleghast, and Froslass that set entry hazards pair naturally, as they help pressure the opponent's team to use Defog. Ghost-types like Hisuian Typhlosion, Chandelure, and Decidueye make for good partners, as they can create a hazard removal-punishing duo because any of them can spinblock, and Tornadus can punish Defoggers. Tornadus can have issues with KOing Steel-types like Registeel, Bronzong, and Orthworm, meaning teammates like Munkidori, Diancie, Cinccino, and Minior have great synergy, since they can work alongside Tornadus to overwhelm these shared checks. Cinccino is especially good thanks to its Tidy Up clearing Stealth Rock for Tornadus. Fighting- and Ground-types such as Breloom, Toxicroak, Torterra, Paldean Tauros-W, and Flygon work well to take out the aforementioned Steel-types as well as Rock-types like Diancie. The former three can also help take care of pesky defensive Water-types like Vaporeon, Milotic, and Swampert. Bulk Up Tornadus struggles with OHKOing Alolan Ninetales and breaking through Ice-types like Avalugg, meaning teammates that can switch in and beat them such as Chandelure and Diancie are greatly appreciated.

movesets.name: Nasty Plot
movesets.description:
Set Details

Hurricane provides Tornadus with more power, but Bleakwind Storm has higher accuracy. Focus Blast allows Tornadus to better hit Rock-types like Diancie as well as Dark-types like Incineroar, but Heat Wave gives it a more reliable way of taking out Steel-types such as Copperajah and Registeel. Dark Pulse lets Tornadus hit Wind Rider Brambleghast and the Fighting-neutral Bronzong super effectively, which could potentially wall Tornadus otherwise. Alternatively, Tera Blast Steel can be run to super effectively hit Diancie, which would wall Tornadus pretty well otherwise, as well as letting Tornadus KO Brambleghast. Tera Steel also means Tornadus can take attacks like Inteleon's Ice Beam, Cinccino's Tail Slap, and Munkidori's Psychic, giving it an easier time setting up and firing off attacks. Tera Ground, on the other hand, allows Tornadus to better take on Rock- and Electric-types like Diancie and Kilowattrel. Tera Dark can also potentially be used, as it boosts Dark Pulse and allows Tornadus to have an easier time breaking through Uxie and Bronzong.

Tornadus enjoys partners like Diancie, Munkidori, Uxie, Calm Mind Scream Tail, and Porygon-Z, as they can help to overwhelm shared Steel-type checks like Bronzong, Copperajah, and Registeel. Cinccino is also quite good at this, and it can remove entry hazards for Tornadus, letting it comfortably run a different item. Pokemon like Diancie, Toxtricity, and Weakness Policy Incineroar help bring in Fighting- and Ground-types like Breloom, Flygon, and Swampert, which all give Tornadus free setup opportunities. Since Tornadus will most likely thud into and faint to a Steel- or Rock-type, a teammate like Chandelure, Breloom, Torterra, or Flygon works well to take advantage of the free entry they get afterwards. A dedicated lead like Booster Energy Scream Tail, Brambleghast, Eject Pack Flygon, or Focus Sash Infernape is also appreciated to help wear down Tornadus's checks like Diancie, Registeel, and Alolan Muk.

movesets.name: Bulky Tailwind
movesets.description:
• Tornadus takes advantage of a combination of Prankster and Tailwind to set nearly uncontested speed control. This allows it to ensure that its teammates can move first and remove or cripple threats before they can move.
  • Bleakwind Storm allows Tornadus to take on an offensive presence, even after using up all of its support moves.
  • Taunt is the best option for the third moveslot, as it can disrupt the foes' ability to use status moves, effectively crippling support options and ameliorating the risk of a foe setting up or inflicting status. However, priority Rain Dance and Sunny Day can be strong options for teams that are more weather dependent, and they can be beneficial for teams that are afraid of weather by providing the ability to reverse the opponent's weather.
  • Protect allows Tornadus to survive an attack that can potentially KO it or delay setting up Tailwind. This can be particularly useful in Tailwind mirror matches, as setting Tailwind a turn later can allow for an extra turn where your team has Tailwind and the opponent's doesn't. If needed, this slot can be used for weather setting, but losing Protect can make it significantly more difficult for Tornadus to set Tailwind multiple times throughout the match.
  • Covert Cloak allows Tornadus to safely set up Tailwind against Fake Out users such as Rillaboom and Incineroar. Note that Covert Cloak and Tera Ghost should not be used together, since they effectively do the same thing. Sitrus Berry can be used to boost Tornadus's long-term survivability, allowing it to set Tailwind multiple times per match.
  • Tera Steel is an excellent defensive type, and it boosts Tornadus's survivability by giving it a resistance to lethal Ice-type attacks from Chien-Pao and Kyurem as well as common attacks from Pokemon like Gholdengo, Tornadus, Dragonite, and Glimmora. On the other hand, Tera Ghost and Tera Dark both prevent foes from disrupting Tornadus's support options by blocking Fake Out or Prankster Taunt, respectively.
  • Tornadus's bulk allows it to survive significantly more than the other Prankster Tailwind setters. Tornadus needs to maximize its physical bulk in order to survive a Wild Charge from Assault Vest Iron Hands without needing to Terastallize. The physical bulk also allows Tornadus to set Tailwind multiple times per game and allows it to survive physical priority moves that can outprioritize and prevent Tailwind, such as Dragonite's Extremespeed.
  • Tornadus pairs best with offensive threats that have middling Speed. Pokemon such as Gholdengo and Regidrago can take advantage of the boosted speed to outspeed major threats such as opposing Landorus and Chien-Pao.

movesets.name: Focus Sash
movesets.description:
• Tornadus is the defining Tailwind user in the DOU metagame. Prankster allows Tornadus to set Tailwind with an incredible degree of consistency. This, combined with its high Special Attack and Bleakwind Storm, has made Tornadus a cornerstone in offensive team compositions.

  • Bleakwind Storm allows Tornadus to threaten the metagame's numerous common Grass-types, among them Ogerpon-W and Sinistcha.

  • Running Focus Sash allows maximum investment into Special Attack and Speed. Critically, having maximum Speed enables Tornadus to outspeed and pressure Ogerpon-W and -H.

  • Icy Wind provides another means of speed control. Though normally quite weak, it is able to 2HKO Landorus, one of the most common Pokemon in the metagame. The damage is also significant against the tier's many Focus Sash users, most notably Glimmora, Chien-Pao, and opposing Tornadus, breaking their Focus Sashes while simultaneously dropping their Speed and allowing Tornadus's partner to follow up. This move is most effective against opposing offensive Tailwind-based teams, as stacking both forms of speed control provides the edge against a team with just Tailwind.

  • Taunt shuts down many support-oriented Pokemon entirely, preventing them from using highly disruptive moves like Spore, Trick Room, and Tailwind. Though because of Prankster, it is unable to affect Dark-types such as Incineroar and Ting-Lu and is blocked by Armor Tail and Psychic Terrain.

  • Sunny Day activates Protosynthesis and boosts Fire-type attackers such as Chi-Yu and Ogerpon-H. Similarly, Rain Dance supports Water-types like Ogerpon-W in addition to increasing the accuracy of Bleakwind Storm and Sandsear Storm. Both of these weather options also have utility in disrupting opposing teams, weakening the corresponding typing and blocking weather-reliant effects like Aurora Veil and Swift Swim.

  • Focus Sash's defensive properties allow Tornadus to forgo a defensive Tera type in favor of the utility of the Ghost typing. Tera Ghost's primary value is in evading Fake Out and the less common Extreme Speed, allowing Tornadus to set Tailwind on a critical turn and resume applying offensive pressure afterwards. In practice, however, Tornadus is not a common user of Terastallization, as it's usually more valuable to save it for one of the team's offensive powerhouses.

  • As Tailwind is a common part of many teams, it is not uncommon to have your Tailwind essentially neutralized by a foe setting their own. In these Tailwind mirror matchups, it's often advised to try and offset your own Tailwind by a turn or two with the aim of having the Speed advantage after their Tailwind has ended. Opting to use Icy Wind can also provide an advantage during matched Tailwinds by lowering the Speed of both foes.

  • Tornadus fits best on teams with offensive Pokemon that need their Speed patched up. Landorus, Gholdengo, and Regidrago are all great examples of offensive powerhouses that find themselves outsped by faster threats such as Chien-Pao and Ogerpon formes. Even slow Pokemon like Iron Hands and Ursaluna-B can greatly benefit from partnering with Tornadus. With some Speed investment, they're able to use the Tailwind to outspeed Landorus and Ogerpon-W while also benefiting from Tornadus's ability to check the Grass-types that trouble them both.

strategies.overview:
• Tornadus is one of the strongest support Pokemon bearing a great toolkit, including Tailwind, Taunt, Rain Dance, and Sunny Day. Prankster provides great speed and weather control. It has a great matchup against Rillaboom and Amoonguss, thanks to Bleakwind Storm, a great spread move which gives it a field presence, and Taunt.

  • Tornadus has amazing synergy with Urshifu-R and fast Pokemon like Flutter Mane, Chien-Pao, and Landorus, which define the archetype of tailwind hyper offense.

  • Tornadus can become vulnerable to certain threats like Urshifu-R, Chien-Pao, and opposing Taunt Tornadus depending on its item choice. Focus Sash struggles against Urshifu-R, and items like Covert Cloak and Mental Herb struggle against Chien-Pao. Rocky Helmet matches poorly into Fake Out and Taunt pressure.

  • Tornadus struggles to create field pressure as a singular Pokemon. It cannot Taunt Pokemon like Farigiraf and Indeedee due to their respective abilities blocking priority. Chien-Pao, Raging Bolt, Iron Hands and Archaludon are bad matchups for it because of their ability to quickly remove it from the field.

movesets.name: Bulky Tailwind
movesets.description:
• Bleakwind Storm provides good damage into Rillaboom and Ogerpon-W. Tailwind is the most effective speed control Tornadus has access to. Taunt helps shut down Amoonguss and helps to manage certain Trick Room Pokemon like Porygon2 and Dusclops, but Protect can be run instead to ensure Tailwind goes up. Rain Dance and Sunny Day serve as weather control, which enables your sweepers and disables opposing weather-based sweepers. Rain Dance pairs well with Urshifu-R and Ogerpon-W while Sunny Day powers up Chi-Yu and Flutter Mane.

  • This given EV spread focuses on bulk, surviving Mystic Water Surging Strikes from Urshifu-R and Tera Fairy Choice Specs Moonblast from Flutter Mane. The low Speed investment ensures that Tornadus sets up its own weather.

  • Rocky Helmet helps against Urshifu-R mirrors and provides good chip into opposing physical attackers making contact. Covert Cloak prevents Fake Out flinches from Incineroar and Rillaboom. It also negates any secondary effects from moves like Rock Slide and Icy Wind. This ensures that Tailwind goes up. Mental Herb helps to shrug off one Taunt.

  • Tera Dark provides an immunity to Prankster Taunt, guaranteeing Tailwind. Tera Steel provides useful resistance to Chien-Pao and Flutter Mane's STAB moves. Both Tera types improve matchups into Psyspam and against Electric-type moves from Pokemon like Raging Bolt, Iron Hands and Archaludon.

movesets.name: Offensive Tailwind
movesets.description:
• Focus Sash ensures Tornadus survives one attack and set up Tailwind. Protect becomes important to avoid Fake Out without committing the Tera early.

  • Tornadus rarely Terastallizes, but Tera Ghost can ensure that it can more reliably set up Tailwind by negating Fake Out from Pokemon like Incineroar and Rillaboom, and Extreme Speed from Pokemon like Dragonite and Entei. Tera Flying increases its offensive pressure.

movesets.name: Tailwind Support
movesets.description:
Tornadus is used as a support Pokemon that can set Tailwind for its team and deal semi-consistent damage with Bleakwind Storm. It is very good into Grass-types such as Amoonguss and Rillaboom, as Tornadus can easily use Taunt or threaten them with Bleakwind Storm. Tornadus can make use of its weather-setting abilities to help itself hit Bleakwind Storms or support its teammates by boosting or reducing the damage of Water- or Fire-type moves. Icy Wind provides a secondary form of speed control for Tornadus and helps against other Tailwind-based teams. Protect can also help against Fake Out if it holds Rocky Helmet. Covert Cloak allows Tornadus to shine as a supportive piece, as it stops it from being flinched by the common Fake Out. It also prevents it from having its Special Attack lowered by Snarl. Rocky Helmet acts more as a repellent for attacks like Urshifu-R's Surging Strikes and Chien-Pao's Ice Spinner. It also can make Pokemon more wary of using Fake Out, as they will be constantly taking chip damage. The EV spread on this Tornadus allows it to take a Tera Water Surging Strikes from Urshifu-R. This can be really impactful on the Rocky Helmet set, as it forces Urshifu-R down to 50% of its health upon hitting it. It can also take an Astral Barrage from Choice Specs Calyrex-S. Tera Dark is mainly used to stop other Tornadus from using Taunt or Whimsicott from using Encore on it. It can also be used as a defensive Tera against Calyrex-S, as it resists or is immune to both of its STAB attacks. Tera Steel can be used to resist attacks from Pokemon such as Chien-Pao and the occasional Rock-type. It also removes a weakness to Electric, which can make it fare better against Raging Bolt.

Tornadus is a good partner for many Pokemon thanks to its ability to support them through speed control and weather. One example of this is Chi-Yu, which makes use of Tornadus's ability to set sun and Tailwind to blast through opposing teams. Chi-Yu also helps Tornadus's Bleakwind Storms do more damage. Kyogre is another good partner, as Tornadus allows it to outspeed non-Tailwind teams with its below average Speed stat. Tornadus can also help to stop other weather teams from outdamaging Kyogre while letting Kyogre deal with opposing weather attackers. Tornadus benefits other Pokemon with its weather as well such as Urshifu-R, Koraidon and Archaludon. It can also provide a check to weather-setting Pokemon like Koraidon and Groudon with opposing weather. Checks to Tornadus include Miraidon and Raging Bolt. Their ability to resist its attacks and fire back with powerful Electric-type STAB moves can threaten both Tornadus and its common partners. One other check is Kingambit. Often, Tornadus cannot attack with Bleakwind Storm due to the threat of Defiant being activated. It can easily set up in front of Tornadus or, if it has Assault Vest, threaten its partner. Landorus, however, can help to beat some of these checks with strong Sandsear Storms in Rain while being immune to Miraidon's and Raging Bolt's Electric-type STAB moves. Trick Room teams are also a bad matchup, as they flip the Speed stats and make Tailwind useless. Calyrex-I is especially tough for Tornadus, as it can target it down with strong Glacial Lances or set Trick Room right in front of it.

movesets.name: Bulky Tailwind
movesets.description:
Set Details

  • Tornadus is one of two viable priority Tailwind setters in the metagame, pairing excellently with Restricted Pokemon like Calyrex-S, Zamazenta-C, and Kyogre that appreciate its combination of weather control, speed control, and Flying-type STAB moves that allow it to threaten Restricted Pokemon like Koraidon as well as non-Restricted Pokemon like Amoonguss, Rillaboom, and the Urshifu formes.
  • Bleakwind Storm is used for strong spread Flying-type STAB damage, while Hurricane is chosen to hit through the Wide Guard used by Zamazenta and Lunala while securing an OHKO on the Urshifu formes. Hurricane is only an option on Kyogre teams due to its inconsistency outside of rain. Rain Dance deactivates Koraidon's Orichalcum Pulse and significantly weakens its Fire-type moves while also setting up the rain for its own Water-type partners like Urshifu-R and Kyogre. Taunt is chosen to prevent status moves like Zamazenta-C's Wide Guard, Amoonguss's Spore, and Calyrex-I or Lunala's Trick Room that would disable or take advantage of Tornadus and its partners, Kyogre and Calyrex-S. Generally, Tornadus runs Protect on non-Covert Cloak sets in order to avoid flinches from Fake Out or on offensive teams that do not need Rain Dance and would prefer the increased staying power generated by Protect.
  • Covert Cloak is chosen to allow Tornadus to set up Tailwind against Fake Out Pokemon like Incineroar and Rillaboom that would otherwise leave it vulnerable to being KOed or pressure it into using Protect . Rocky Helmet is chosen in order to allow Tornadus to punish Urshifu-R and Koraidon, forcing them to take significant recoil.
  • The Speed investment allows Tornadus to outspeed maximum Speed Groudon and Kyogre, while the bulk investment allows Tornadus to survive Tera Water Surging Strikes from Urshifu-R or Thunderclap from Raging Bolt.
  • Tera Dark is chosen to allow Tornadus to block Taunt from opposing Tornadus and Encore from opposing Whimsicott, while also providing it a key resistance to Calyrex-S's STAB moves.

Teambuilding

  • Raging Bolt and Miraidon threaten to OHKO Tornadus with their STAB Electric-type moves, being able to OHKO it with a Special Attack Protosynthesis-boosted Thunderclap, which takes Tornadus out before it can move, or Volt Switch, which creates momentum for the opposing team, respectively. Tornadus also hates Pokemon that are able to set up Trick Room against it while threatening to OHKO it, with Restricted Pokemon like Calyrex-I and Meteor Beam Lunala being able dissuade Tornadus's Taunt with their offensive pressure. Indeedee-F and Farigaraf also present unique challenges to Tornadus, as the two of them are able to set up Trick Room while also blocking Tornadus's Prankster Taunt with their abilities. While Tornadus can OHKO Whimsicott, its Speed combined with Prankster Encore allow it to shut down Tornadus and punish it for using Tailwind or prevent it altogether with Taunt.
  • Urshifu-R is Tornadus's premier partner, being able to take advantage of both the Tailwind and Rain Dance it sets up in order to do massive damage uncontested by Protect. Rillaboom is able to contest Indeedee-F and Miraidon's Terrains, threatening the former and switching in on the latter while also applying Fake Out pressure, allowing Tornadus to more effectively set Tailwind throughout the course of a game. Landorus is notable for its ability to OHKO both Raging Bolt and Miraidon while appreciating Tornadus's Tailwind allowing it to outspeed threats like Calyrex-S, Zamazenta-C, and the aforementioned Miraidon.
  • Kyogre is another of Tornadus's primary partners, with Tornadus being able to hit Grass-types like Rillaboom, Amoonguss, and the Ogerpon formes super effectively with its Flying-type attacks for it while also being able to reset rain into opposing weather control. Tornadus appreciates Kyogre's ability to output immense damage into Trick Room setters like Calyrex-I, Lunala, Farigiraf, and Indeedee-F, allowing it to freely set Tailwind for its partners. Calyrex-S also greatly appreciates Tornadus's Tailwind, which allows it to gain an advantage against opposing Calyrex-S and Koraidon. Tornadus's Taunt support is vital for both Restricted Pokemon, as it is able to prevent Zamazenta-C and Lunala from using Wide Guard. Zacian-C is a also a notable partner because it appreciates Tornadus's ability to set Tailwind against Miraidon and Calyrex-S while taking advantage of its ability to set rain in the face of Koraidon. Zacian-C is also able to handle a lot of Tornadus's checks, since it is able to outspeed and OHKO Raging Bolt, Miraidon, and most Calyrex-I.

movesets.name: Offensive Support
movesets.description:
Set Details

  • Sharp Beak Tornadus is a bulky offensive support Pokemon that can output decent damage with Bleakwind Storm. It has positive matchups versus various metagame staples, such as Koraidon, Rillaboom, and Amoonguss, as well as good neutral matchups into much more of the metagame.
  • Taunt provides disruption, denying otherwise crippling plays from opposing supporting moves; it's especially helpful for Trick Room and Wide Guard users, since negating those allow Tailwind and Bleakwind Storm to be effective.
  • Sharp Beak lets Tornadus be more flexible, since it will be able to deal good chip damage even when Taunted; this allows Tornadus to run more bulk. With the Sharp Beak, it has a chance to OHKO Koraidon and 2HKOes Amoonguss and Rillaboom.
  • The Defense and HP investment allows Tornadus to live a Behemoth Blade from +1 Zacian-C and a Surging Strikes from Mystic Water Urshifu-R; the Special Defense investment allows Tornadus to survive an Astral Barrage or a Psychic from a Life Orb Calyrex-S. The Speed investment lets Tornadus outspeed the entire unboosted metagame under Tailwind, as well as letting partner Smeargle outspeed and use Decorate on Tornadus, letting +2 Tornadus 2HKO bulky Pokemon like Zamazenta-C. The remaining EVs are invested into Special Attack.
  • Tera Dragon lets it live a Water Spout in rain from Kyogre, a Flare Blitz from Koraidon in sun, a Meteor Beam from Lunala, or an Overheat from Modest Chi-Yu.

Teambuilding

  • Tornadus dislikes opposing Whimsicott, since a Taunt or Encore will largely limit Tornadus's usefulness. It's also susceptible to Fake Out users like Incineroar and Iron Hands, as it doesn't have Covert Cloak or Tera Ghost.
  • Tornadus is countered by Raging Bolt, Miraidon, and Calyrex-I, all of which threaten OHKOs on Tornadus both before and after Terastallizing and can easily take Bleakwind Storms multiple times.
  • Tornadus appreciates Smeargle, since Smeargle can redirect dangerous Electro Drifts, Thunderclaps, and Thunderbolts from Miraidon and Raging Bolt, respectively, and can block opposing Glacial Lances, Water Spouts, and Origin Pulses from Calyrex-I and Kyogre, respectively, with Wide Guard.
  • Restricted Pokémon like Zamazenta-C, Calyrex-S, and Kyogre appreciate being around Tornadus, since it can let them outspeed everything with Tailwind, excluding Speed Booster Energy Iron Treads and Flutter Mane. Tornadus can also deny opposing Wide Guard with Taunt, letting Calyrex-S and Kyogre freely fire off Astral Barrage and Water Spout, respectively.
  • Rillaboom acts as a check to Raging Bolt and Miraidon, easily tanking Electric-type damage for Tornadus while getting rid of Electric Terrain. It is also important Fake Out support that moves before Incineroar and Iron Hands.
  • Raging Bolt is also a wonderful partner for Tornadus, since they cover each other great defensively and together have nigh-unresisted coverage; additionally, Raging Bolt can revenge kill Miraidon and opposing Raging Bolt after Tailwind has been set up.

movesets.name: Tailwind
movesets.description:
Tornadus is one of the tier's best support Pokemon, providing crucial speed control with Prankster-boosted Tailwind while still having respectable damage output with Bleakwind Storm. Taunt allows Tornadus to shut down foes like Amoonguss and prevent Pokemon like Porygon2 from setting Trick Room. The given EV spread allows Tornadus to live a Psycho Boost from Deoxys-A, and the remaining EVs are dumped into Special Attack. Covert Cloak is used to nullify the flinching effect of Fake Out, allowing Tornadus to set up Tailwind without worrying about foes such as Incineroar and Iron Hands stopping it. Alternatively, Tera Ghost can be used for a similar effect, additionally granting Tornadus immunity to Extreme Speed from foes such as Dragonite and Entei. If Tera Ghost is used, Sitrus Berry should be used to increase Tornadus's survivability. Tera Steel provides Tornadus with a resistance to Rock-type coverage, such as Rock Slide from foes like Tyranitar and Landorus-T. Tornadus struggles against Pokemon such as Gholdengo and Raging Bolt, as they resist Bleakwind Storm and can threaten back with massive damage, so Ground-types like both Landorus formes can help. Weather-setting moves like Rain Dance and Sunny Day are options over Protect on weather teams, ensuring weather can stay up.

Notable Partners

Offensive Threats: Generally strong offensive Pokemon appreciate Tornadus's ability to set Tailwind, as offensive teams can make use of Tailwind the best. Additionally, offensive teams appreciate the chip damage that Tornadus deals with Bleakwind Storm, and the prevention of Trick Room with Taunt.

Support Pokemon: Pokemon that appreciate Prankster like Amoonguss are good partners for Tornadus due to it helping them fulfill their role as support Pokemon better, such as giving Amoonguss’s Spore priority.

Water-, Electric-, and Ground-types: Teammates like Ogerpon-W, Iron Hands, and both Landorus formes appreciate Tornadus’s ability to threaten the many common Grass-type foes such as Amoonguss, Rillaboom, Ogerpon-W, and Sinistcha, with Landorus in particular benefitting from being able to use Bleakwind Storm.

strategies.overview:
Draft Order: Round 7 onwards

Price Range: 4-5 points

Overview: With solid Speed and strong mixed offenses, Tornadus can fill the role of an offensive pivot while providing some utility and potentially setting up for a sweep. The combination of Knock Off and U-turn allows it to force progress on almost any foe, and its strong mixed attacking stats can help it chip down many defensive switch-ins. As a secondary role, it can be a setup sweeper using Nasty Plot or Bulk Up along with strong coverage moves. However, it is held back by poor defenses, a lack of accurate and reliable STAB moves, no recovery as a Pokemon weak to Stealth Rock, and an awkward move pool. It is generally outclassed by other Flying-types that have better survivability and utility.
strategies.comments:
Common Roles

Offensive Utility / Pivot: Tornadus's Speed tier and access to Knock Off and U-turn let it function as an excellent offensive pivot. It can use Taunt on passive switch-ins and use Knock Off to remove pesky items like Heavy-Duty Boots and Leftovers. Bleakwind Storm or Hurricane in combination with a coverage move lets it chip down potential switch-ins and wear them out before pivoting out with U-turn.

Setup Sweeper: Access to priority Substitute, Nasty Plot, and Bulk Up along with a solid Speed tier means Tornadus can sweep a weakened team. It can use Prankster with Bulk Up to boost its Defense and Attack before physical attackers can hit it or Nasty Plot to take advantage of its special coverage options. Priority Substitute in combination with another setup move like Bulk Up and recovery in Leftovers can let Tornadus safely set up against its foe.

Common Moves

Primary STAB Moves: Acrobatics, Hurricane, Bleakwind Storm

Setup Moves: Nasty Plot, Bulk Up, Agility

Utility Moves: U-turn, Knock Off, Taunt, Substitute, Brick Break

Coverage: Dark Pulse, Psychic, Heat Wave, Crunch, Sludge Wave, Weather Ball, Grass Knot, Focus Blast, Icy Wind

Niche Moves

Tailwind: With Prankster, Tornadus can reliably set Tailwind. This can be helpful to stop opposing setup sweepers by letting its teammates outspeed them.

Rain Dance: Tornadus can use Prankster to set rain at +1 priority, shutting down opponents' weather and giving Tornadus an accurate Hurricane and coverage with Weather Ball.

Foul Play: Tornadus can threaten a boosted physical attacker by using Foul Play, though it may need a Choice Scarf to outspeed it or bulk investment to survive an attack.

Fling: Fling lets Tornadus deal massive damage with Big Nugget or paralyze foes with Light Ball. It then can use Acrobatics, benefitting from holding no item.

Common Items

Heavy-Duty Boots: Tornadus wants to be switching in and out constantly, and with a weakness to Stealth Rock, it can be chipped down very quickly.Heavy-Duty Boots lets it last longer and find more pivot opportunities.

Choice Specs: Tornadus can make use of Choice Specs and its coverage moves to threaten KOs on many switch-ins that otherwise would survive multiple attacks.

Other Damage-boosting Items: Expert Belt, Life Orb, and Sharp Beak can all be used to boost Tornadus's damage output without locking it into a move.

Niche Items

No Item: If Stealth Rock isn't an issue in a matchup, running no item allows Tornadus to take advantage of STAB Acrobatics without having to get rid of its item first.

Sitrus Berry: On bulkier or setup sets, Sitrus Berry can both restore health and get rid of Tornadus's item, turning Acrobatics into a powerful STAB attack.

Big Nugget / Light Ball: Fling becomes a valuable tool for Tornadus when used with Big Nugget or Light Ball: Big Nugget lets it act as a powerful Dark-type nuke, while Light Ball gives it utility by paralyzing the foe.

Leftovers: Bulky sets can use Leftovers with priority Substitute and Bulk Up to let Tornadus heal behind a Substitute while setting up.

Choice Scarf: While Tornadus has a solid Speed tier, there are many threats that are faster than it. Outspeeding them lets it pivot more safely or even KO them with a super effective move.

Tera

Tornadus is a solid option for a secondary Tera Captain in combination with a higher-cost Tera Captain. It uses offensive Tera types best to boost its wallbreaking power or give it more coverage options. It can use Tera Flying to gain an accurate STAB move or further boost Bleakwind Storm and Hurricane, or it can expand on its coverage with Tera Ice or Electric. Tera Ground gives it a super effective move against Electric-, Rock-, and Steel-types, and Tera Fighting gives it an accurate special Fighting-type move or adds even more power to Focus Blast. It can also use defensive Tera types like Tera Poison, Steel, and Water to give it more setup opportunities.

Draft Strategy

Tornadus is a Pokemon that you pick up late in the draft to patch holes in your team. It provides a valuable Ground immunity, and it should mostly function as an offensive pivot to support your stronger Pokemon. It can wear down checks with Knock Off and U-turn, prevent setup or disrupt passive Pokemon with Taunt, and use strong Hurricanes or Bleakwind Storms to chip away at the opposing team. Tornadus is best as a cheap role-filler that won't be brought to every game but can really put in work in specific matchups.

Bulky Steel-types: Tornadus resists Fighting and is immune to Ground-type moves, while bulky Steel-types can switch in on Rock- and Ice-type moves that threaten it in return. Empoleon, Archaludon, and Heatran all appreciate Tornadus's ability to pivot around them and switch into moves that threaten them.

Entry Hazard Setters: Knock Off removes opposing Heavy-Duty Boots, letting your team get more value out of entry hazards and chipping down the opposing team. Setup sets appreciate a worn-down opposing team that can be more easily swept after a single boost. Entry hazard setters like Jirachi, Gastrodon, and Sandy Shocks all appreciate having a Knock Off pivot to help them force progress. Tornadus also has access to Defiant to punish opponents using Defog as their form of hazard removal.

Entry Hazard Removal: Tornadus doesn't always want to be running Heavy-Duty Boots, so it needs solid entry hazard removal to make sure it doesn't get chipped down by Stealth Rock. Pokemon like Excadrill, Iron Treads, and Tentacruel can remove hazards to ensure Tornadus can come in safely with more offensive items.

Slow Pivots: Pokemon like Scizor and Galarian Slowking that can function as slow pivots are excellent counterparts to Tornadus. They can absorb a hit before switching, letting Tornadus stay on the battlefield longer and switch in more times. Additionally, a Volt Switch user like Rotom-W or Jolteon can form the other half of a VoltTurn core, chipping down foes and pivoting into better matchups.

Checks and Counters

Electric-types: Electric-types can take a hit from Tornadus and threaten to kill it with a STAB attack, forcing it to switch. Raging Bolt, Jolteon, Thundurus-T, and many other Electric-types perform in this role well and can cause problems for Tornadus.

Priority: Tornadus is somewhat frail, and strong super effective priority moves like Ice Shard from Mamoswine and Accelerock from Lycanroc can easily KO it from high health. Additionally, Sucker Punch from Pokemon like Kingambit or even an Extreme Speed from Dragonite can take out Tornadus before it can respond.

Fast Offensive Pokemon: Even neutral attacks from a faster Pokemon can seriously threaten Tornadus's ability to perform in its role. Greninja, Weaville, and Iron Boulder can all switch in and force Tornadus to switch out or be KOed before it can attack back.

Entry Hazards and Knock Off: Stealth Rock can hurt Tornadus's ability to switch in safely, and if its Heavy-Duty Boots get removed with Knock Off, it can no longer freely pivot in and out. Pokemon like Iron Treads and Great Tusk that can both set Stealth Rock and use Knock Off cause problems for it.
